subject: Follow-up: token ceiling impact + streaming routing questions
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex@veridian.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Jul 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: token ceiling impact + streaming routing questions

Alex — great to chat earlier. Thanks for walking us through the Veridian ingestion and summarization flow. Per our discussion, here’s a concise recap and the items we need to close on to size SLOs and routing: 

1) Current expected traffic shape (from your side)
- Peak concurrent users: ~250 (product team estimate)
- Typical request size (input): 4–8k tokens (structured notes + metadata)
- Average generated output: 1.2–2.5k tokens (summaries + highlights)

2) Latency targets you called out
- Interactive UI flows: p95 <= 1.2s for inference (post-request)
- Background batch summarization (async): p95 <= 6s acceptable

3) Streaming requirements
- Primary UX: partial streaming of generated bullets as they’re produced; must start streaming within 300–400ms for short responses, tolerates progressive updates for long outputs

4) Constraints we raised
- If we force a single model with 12k input+output envelope, per-token latency rises sharply on GPUs without KV optimizations. We recommended prefix caching and chunked windowing where possible.

5) Questions for you (action items)
- Can you confirm the 95th percentile of request input sizes (tokens) across last 30 days? You mentioned a spike from batch exports — we need that sample.
- Which routes need strict interactive latency vs. which can tolerate streaming/delayed completion?
- Any regulatory constraints forcing on-prem data processing for summaries?

Attached: the quick SLO matrix we sketched during the call (veridian-slo-matrix.xlsx) and the recording.

Proposed next steps
- You share production token histogram + one week of anonymized request logs (or a representative sample) — target by EOD Wed (2026-07-07).
- We do a short perf micro-benchmark with a 8k/2k envelope to validate p95 on streaming path (Redwood side) — will aim to share results within 48h of receiving sample.
- Tentative follow-up call: Thu 07/09 10am PT to review benchmarks and routing plan.

If that aligns, I’ll loop in Eng (Marcus) to run the micro-bench and Marissa to start drafting SLA language.

Thanks,
Priyom
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Follow-up: token ceiling impact + streaming routing questions

Thanks Priyom — quick answers inline: 

> Can you confirm the 95th percentile of request input sizes (tokens) across last 30 days?
We’re pulling the histogram now. High-level: median ~3.5k, p95 ~9.1k, p99 ~14k (those p99s are mostly batch exports we run nightly for compliance snapshots). Will share a redacted sample by Wednesday.

> Which routes need strict interactive latency vs. which can tolerate streaming/delayed completion?
Primary UI Compose and Live Notes need interactivity (p95 <= 1.2s). The Weekly Digest and Compliance snapshot can be async and run in the background (p95 up to 10s is fine).

> On-prem constraints?
Compliance team prefers data-at-rest in our VPC for customer health records; however initial pilot can use Redwood Dedicated with strict routing to our VPC region.

Also — curious about your recommendation for chunked windowing: how would that impact coherence for our long outputs?

—Alex
Director of Product, Veridian Health

Subject: Fwd: Follow-up: token ceiling impact + streaming routing questions — action items for perf test

Marissa/Marcus — forwarding Alex’s answers. Key points: p95 input ~9.1k, p99 ~14k (batch). They separate interactive vs async routes. Veridian prefers Dedicated/VPC for pilot.

Immediate asks for Eng: 
- Marcus: can you run a micro-benchmark for two envelopes: (A) 8k input / 2k output, (B) 12k input / 2k output on the streaming path. Measure p50/p95/p99 latency and first-streamed-token time. Also test with/without prefix KV caching enabled. Use Redwood Dedicated profile (we can simulate their region hardware). Target: numbers by EOD Wed (07/07).

- Marissa: start a one-page SLA draft that covers interactive p95 <=1.2s (best effort) and async p95 <=10s with explicit fallback (long-run queue) and routing policy notes. Include an item for Dedicated pilot (region + expected throughput).

I’ll prepare the sample ingestion they asked for once Marcus confirms the benchmark config.

Thanks,
Priyom

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex@veridian.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Jul 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: token ceiling impact + streaming routing questions

Alex — thanks for the fast turnaround and for confirming the histograms. Quick readout from Eng (Marcus) attached below and next steps: 

Summary of Marcus’ micro-bench (high level) — attached CSV inside the Drive link: 
- Envelope A (8k in / 2k out): p50 = 320ms, p95 = 1.05s, p99 = 1.8s; first-streamed-token = 160ms 
- Envelope B (12k in / 2k out): p50 = 720ms, p95 = 2.9s, p99 = 5.6s; first-streamed-token = 420ms 

Key takeaways:
- Streaming start time degrades linearly with larger input when KV cache is cold. Enabling prefix caching brings Envelope B p95 down to ~1.6s in our test — big win if Veridian can use a short-lived session cache for repeated context (e.g., multi-turn compose).
- For purely interactive flows, recommend keeping input window to <=9k tokens or applying a quick pre-filtering step to reduce token mass (we can help with a lightweight client-side summarizer).
- Long batch snapshots (p99 at 14k) should run on async routing to a higher-throughput Dedicated pool with relaxed latency SLOs.

Proposed concrete next steps: 
1) We provision a small Dedicated canary in us-west with KV caching enabled for your pilot.
2) Your team shares one week of redacted request logs (per Priyom) so we can simulate exact distributions.
3) Redwood will produce a draft SLA containing interactive and async tiers; we’ll include fallback routing policy and an ops playbook for high-p99 events.

I’ve put the detailed micro-bench CSV and the perf notes in the shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-veridian-slo 

If that looks good, can we lock the pilot start for Monday 07/13?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
